AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: We determined the effect of late-phase responses to allergen challenge of mildly allergic asthmatic patients on the expression and release of the cytokines IL-10 and MIP-1α from peripheral blood monocytes.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Sixteen mildly allergic asthmatics were exposed to increasing concentrations of allergen aerosol. Nine demonstrated an early response alone (single responders), while seven had an early followed by a late response (dual responders). Monocytes were isolated from venous blood before and 24 h after allergen challenge, and placed in short-term culture for determination ofIL-10 mRNA expression by reverse-transcription polymerase chain reactionand protein release. MIP-1α protein release was measured byradioimmunoassay.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: IL-10 mRNA expression was significantly higher in dual responders than early responders alone, for unstimulated monocytes or for monocytes exposed to lipopolysaccharide or IL-1β. In addition, the release of IL-10 and MIP-1α from monocytes of dual responders was also enhanced.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Circulating monocytes are primed to release more of the cytokines, IL-10 and MIP-1α, in dual but not in single responders, at 24 h afterallergen. They may contribute to allergen-induced inflammatory responsesin the airways.
